caption_policy: One artwork identity, one canonical caption. Derivatives and aliases inherit it. Captions may be omitted for decorative placements; never replaced with page-specific copy. Alt text and contextual prose serve different purposes. Historical snapshots retain their original wording.

artworks.title: Pond At Dawn
artworks.caption: The pond holds the morning quietly.
artworks.alt: An intimate view of a rural Odisha pond at dawn.

artworks.title: Kendu Light
artworks.caption: In the woodland, light finds a leaf.
artworks.alt: A small branch of broad oval kendu leaves in an Odisha woodland, a single drop of rain at the edge of a leaf.

artworks.title: Thread By The Window
artworks.caption: A loose thread remembers the hands.
artworks.alt: An everyday corner in an Odisha home: a folded handwoven Sambalpuri sari with a restrained ivory and indigo geometric ikat border lies on a low wooden stool.

artworks.title: Koraput Morning
artworks.caption: The hills leave room for a breath.
artworks.alt: A narrow earthen footpath through dewy grass on a misty Koraput hillside in Odisha, soft blue-green ridges receding, a single small wildflower near the path.

artworks.title: Courtyard Petals
artworks.caption: A few petals. The afternoon stays.
artworks.alt: A sunlit earthen courtyard corner in Odisha after a brief shower, weathered warm laterite wall, a few fallen magenta bougainvillea petals beside a tiny pale puddle.

artworks.title: Sea Breeze Cloth
artworks.caption: The breeze carries what words leave behind.
artworks.alt: A small off-white and muted red checked cotton gamucha hanging loosely on a simple timber rail near Odisha's coast.

artworks.title: Quiet Path
artworks.caption: The path continues, softly.
artworks.alt: A red-earth path winds between grass and distant hills.

artworks.title: Correspondence
artworks.caption: Some words wait by the window.
artworks.alt: A sealed letter rests at a rain-speckled blue window.

artworks.title: Reader Letters
artworks.caption: A little warmth between the words.
artworks.alt: Letters and an earthen teacup rest on a small wooden stool.

artworks.title: Reading Room
artworks.caption: A page makes room for silence.
artworks.alt: An open notebook lies on a blue bench beside still water.

artworks.title: Voices
artworks.caption: A place kept for another voice.
artworks.alt: Three empty cane chairs gather beneath a flowering tree.

artworks.title: Writer Profile
artworks.caption: The chair remembers a presence.
artworks.alt: An empty cane chair holds a notebook beside a quiet window.

artworks.title: Our Story
artworks.caption: The threshold remembers home.
artworks.alt: An Odisha home with a blue door, earthen courtyard and threshold drawings.

artworks.title: Gatherings
artworks.caption: There is room to sit together.
artworks.alt: A shaded veranda has woven stools and an empty wooden chair.

artworks.title: Archive
artworks.caption: Time rests between the pages.
artworks.alt: Old clothbound books, a dried leaf and a cotton bookmark.

artworks.title: Book Reviews
artworks.caption: A page waits for the light.
artworks.alt: An open book with spectacles and a cup on a wooden table.

artworks.title: Editorial Desk
artworks.caption: The unwritten line is still listening.
artworks.alt: Blank sheets, pencils and a notebook in soft window light.

artworks.title: Next Issue
artworks.caption: A leaf opens beside a page.
artworks.alt: A closed notebook and a branch of young green leaves.

artworks.title: Search
artworks.caption: Beyond the window, an open horizon.
artworks.alt: An open blue window looks onto reeds, water and a distant horizon.

artworks.title: Send A Poem
artworks.caption: A quiet page, ready for a voice.
artworks.alt: An open blank notebook and a fountain pen on folded cotton.

artworks.title: Dokana
artworks.caption: A closed doorway. Rain holds the silence.
artworks.alt: A closed indigo shop shutter above a rain-dark earth threshold.

artworks.title: Kshanika
artworks.caption: An empty platform, waiting with the rain.
artworks.alt: An empty railway platform and bench recede into monsoon mist.

artworks.title: Drink
artworks.caption: A cup by the window; the night gathers on the water.
artworks.alt: An earthen cup at a timber window overlooking quiet evening water.

artworks.title: After the rain
artworks.caption: Everyday Odisha: rain, earthen courtyards and the sensory memory of home.
artworks.alt: A single fallen ivory frangipani flower on wet red laterite earth, small deep teal puddle reflecting an overcast sky, exquisite low macro perspective.

artworks.title: The colour before the story
artworks.caption: Raghurajpur is known for pattachitra, a painting tradition on prepared cloth. This is an imagined workshop and an original border study.
artworks.alt: An artist uses a fine brush to paint an original floral border on cloth, inspired by Raghurajpur.

artworks.title: Evening on the water
artworks.caption: Odisha's lagoon landscapes and fishing livelihoods; an imagined waterside scene, not an identified boat or community.
artworks.alt: A single empty narrow wooden fishing boat among sparse reeds on a tranquil Odisha lagoon at blue hour, wide quiet water seen in a vertical composition, ochre rope on the bow.

artworks.title: A threshold in rain
artworks.caption: Jhoti and chita provide the visual reference: restrained white threshold drawing within an imagined earthen home.
artworks.alt: A simple earthen Odisha courtyard threshold with delicate white rice-paste Jhoti drawing, monsoon rain, a brass water vessel beside a laterite-red wall, no people.

artworks.title: Room for water
artworks.caption: Everyday earthenware and the labour of pottery; no specific craft cluster is claimed for this imagined scene.
artworks.alt: Three handmade terracotta water pitchers drying beside a low mud wall, an indigo cotton cloth, a small pool of window light in a traditional Odisha pottery workspace.

artworks.title: The wind reads first
artworks.caption: Odisha's coastal landscape, interpreted through casuarina, sand and sea air.
artworks.alt: A windswept casuarina on an empty Odisha coastal beach, deep sea-blue waves beyond, pale sand, muted ochre needles, quiet midday haze.

artworks.title: A small red insistence
artworks.caption: Palash provides the botanical and seasonal starting point; the emotional reading is original.
artworks.alt: A few rust-red palasha blossoms on a slender branch against a distant hazy Odisha hillside, dry ochre grasses and blue shadow, realistic botanical intimacy.

artworks.title: The loom remembers a voice
artworks.caption: An imaginative homage to Gangadhar Meher, the Odia poet born into a weaver family in Barpali. This is not his documented loom or workshop.
artworks.alt: A handloom with restrained ivory, rust and deep teal ikat cotton threads in an Odisha weaving room, shallow focus, tactile wood and soft side light, no lettering and no people.

artworks.title: Before the field wakes
artworks.caption: Rice cultivation and rural mornings in Odisha; an imagined field, without assigning it to a named village.
artworks.alt: An ivory veil of dawn mist above harvested paddy fields, one low haystack and a distant palm in rural Odisha, muted ochre stubble and blue-green shadows.

artworks.title: Enough light for one room
artworks.caption: An everyday earthen oil lamp, approached through intimacy rather than a claim about a particular ceremony.
artworks.alt: A tiny unlit terracotta oil lamp on a timeworn laterite niche beside an ivory wall, deep blue twilight outside, understated warm ambient light without theatrical glow.

artworks.title: A boat for remembering
artworks.caption: A poetic reference to Kartika boat-floating traditions in Odisha; an imagined contemporary paper boat, not a reconstruction of an ancient vessel.
artworks.alt: Two handmade paper boats with a single marigold each resting near the edge of an Odisha river at dawn, Kartika seasonal mood, teal reflection and ochre silt, intimate still life.

artworks.title: The season in white
artworks.caption: Kans grass and the changing seasonal landscape; no single festival is asserted by the image.
artworks.alt: Kans grass plumes beside a narrow rural path after the rains in Odisha, ivory feathery grasses against deep blue-green distance, a small patch of rust-red soil.

artworks.title: Not yet a flower
artworks.caption: Lotus and pond life, familiar across Odisha and beyond; the narrative concerns anticipation rather than ritual symbolism.
artworks.alt: An ivory lotus bud rising through broad rain-speckled lotus leaves on a quiet Odisha pond, teal water and subdued earthy reflections, close natural study.

artworks.title: Rain on the tiles
artworks.caption: Terracotta roof tiles and a sheltered courtyard offer a study of everyday domestic architecture in Odisha.
artworks.alt: Rain running down the edge of old terracotta roof tiles above an Odisha courtyard, gentle teal distant blur, an ivory cloth drying in shelter, quietly realistic.

artworks.title: The bowl holds a note
artworks.caption: Kantilo has a brass and bell-metal craft tradition. This concept specifically concerns kansa, bell-metal, rather than treating all yellow metals as interchangeable.
artworks.alt: A softly gleaming kansa bowl, a resting hand and a hammer on a workshop bench.

artworks.title: When the lane turns fragrant
artworks.caption: The scent of rain on earth anchors the brand's ମାଟିର ମହକ theme through everyday experience.
artworks.alt: First rain touching parched red earth in an Odisha village lane, small puddles, ochre dust becoming mud, low intimate perspective, teal-grey cloud reflection.

artworks.title: Summer, carried home
artworks.caption: Mango season and the everyday culture of bringing food home; no named cultivar or local origin is claimed.
artworks.alt: Green mangoes and one ripe ochre mango in a small woven palm basket under a tree, mottled ivory sunlight on red earth, quiet Odisha summer afternoon.

artworks.title: Salt in the cotton
artworks.caption: Puri gamucha is the user's everyday cultural reference. This imagined cotton cloth is not presented as a certified weave, temple-issued cloth or prescribed ritual garment.
artworks.alt: An ivory cotton gamucha with red checks dries on a wooden rail beside the sea.

artworks.title: What the woodland holds
artworks.caption: Kendu woodland generally, as clarified by the user. Kendu leaves are an important forest produce and livelihood connection in Odisha; no particular forest or community is depicted.
artworks.alt: A narrow path passes through kendu woodland beneath rounded green leaves.

artworks.title: The sari keeps the river
artworks.caption: Sambalpuri bandha is a tie-and-dye weaving tradition. This is generated textile interpretation, not an authenticated artisan sample or evidence of a particular motif's meaning.
artworks.alt: A teal Sambalpuri bandha-inspired sari with ivory woven patterns and a red border draped over a stool.

artworks.title: The net before morning
artworks.caption: Coastal fishing work provides the setting; the scene avoids assigning a livelihood or identity to an invented named community.
artworks.alt: A neatly coiled ochre fishing net on the edge of a small wooden boat in an Odisha coastal village, deep blue water and weathered terracotta-toned wood, no people.

artworks.title: The warmth that stays
artworks.caption: The hearth and earthen kitchen express domestic memory; warmth is the subject, without idealising the burdens of cooking or fuel collection.
artworks.alt: A simple rural Odisha earthen cooking hearth, a clay pot, delicate real smoke drifting into cool window light, warm ochre straw and soot-blue shadows, no people.

artworks.title: Steps down to the day
artworks.caption: River steps and water-carrying as an imagined everyday setting; no particular ghat or ritual is identified.
artworks.alt: Quiet old stone steps descending to an Odisha river at early morning, one small brass vessel, deep teal water, soft ivory sky reflection, laterite embankment.

artworks.title: One flower after another
artworks.caption: Flower-threading and everyday acts of welcome and offering; no specific festival or sacred obligation is asserted.
artworks.alt: A short unfinished thread of muted saffron marigolds laid on an old blue wooden ledge, ivory cotton and red clay floor, natural intimate still life in Odisha.

artworks.title: The sky comes to the field
artworks.caption: Flooded paddy fields provide the Odisha agrarian reference; this is an imagined scene, not a record of a particular farm.
artworks.alt: A flooded paddy field reflecting pale monsoon sky, young rice rows and a small ochre earthen bund cutting a graceful curve through teal water, rural Odisha.

artworks.title: Someone will be back
artworks.caption: A bicycle and a lived-in wall suggest everyday mobility and neighbourhood life, without turning poverty or age into decoration.
artworks.alt: A weathered ordinary bicycle resting against an old laterite village wall, a faded sea-blue door, monsoon foliage and a single ivory towel, no people.

artworks.title: The leaf lets go
artworks.caption: A banana leaf after rainfall; a close natural study linked to gardens and familiar household landscapes.
artworks.alt: A broad banana leaf holding clear raindrops above an Odisha courtyard, deep teal-green shade and a blurred red earthen wall, sculptural close photographic composition.

artworks.title: The swing waits for laughter
artworks.caption: A village swing and remembered play. It can suggest Odisha's seasonal celebrations without claiming that the depicted scene documents a specific festival.
artworks.alt: An empty simple rope swing beneath a large rural Odisha tree before monsoon, ochre rope, muted indigo shadows, reddish earth and ivory humid sky, no people.

artworks.title: The tree's patient gift
artworks.caption: Jackfruit in a home landscape; an original reflection on growth and shared food, without assigning a particular recipe or ritual.
artworks.alt: A freshly cut small section of jackfruit on a dark wooden board beside a brass bowl, natural ochre fruit, cool sea-blue window shadow, quiet Odisha home still life.

artworks.title: A breeze made by hand
artworks.caption: A palm-leaf hand fan and everyday craft; the imagined object is not attributed to a named maker or village.
artworks.alt: A handwoven palm-leaf fan resting on an ivory cotton mat by a low red-earth threshold, hot afternoon softened by deep teal doorway shade, lived-in Odisha home.

artworks.title: A forest breathing softly
artworks.caption: Similipal's forests, streams, orchids and ferns ground this imagined ecological study. It is not a documentary photograph of a surveyed spot or a verified orchid species.
artworks.alt: Small orchids, ferns and a mossy tree beside a rocky forest stream, an imagined Similipal scene.

artworks.title: A language looks back
artworks.caption: An interpretive tribute to Fakir Mohan Senapati and his attention to common people in Odia prose. The narrative is original, not a quotation, historical scene or claim about this edition's contents.
artworks.alt: An interpretive portrait of Fakir Mohan Senapati, with swept white hair, an attentive gaze and a dark coat.

artworks.title: What the hands have gathered
artworks.caption: Rice harvest and agricultural labour; gratitude does not erase the work or uncertainty that produced it.
artworks.alt: A carefully tied small sheaf of harvested rice resting on a red laterite courtyard floor, low winter sunlight, ivory husks and cool sea-blue shade, tactile natural detail.

artworks.title: The chair keeps a little warmth
artworks.caption: Domestic cloth, winter light and remembered companionship; an imagined home, not a named person's belongings.
artworks.alt: A simple handwoven ochre and ivory shawl draped over an old wooden chair next to a deep sea-blue door in an Odisha home, winter morning light, no people.

artworks.title: A second moon
artworks.caption: An imagined Odisha lagoon at night; the emotional story concerns distance and companionship.
artworks.alt: A shallow Odisha lagoon under a pale rising moon, a few gentle ripples and distant reeds, deep sea-blue, ivory reflections, almost abstract but photographically realistic.

artworks.title: The morning gathers quietly
artworks.caption: Night-flowering jasmine provides the floral starting point; the image does not claim a particular local devotional practice.
artworks.alt: A delicate white shiuli flower with rust-orange stem resting beside others on a damp laterite-red garden path, autumn morning, intimate realistic low viewpoint.

artworks.title: The rain can stay outside
artworks.caption: A thatched veranda evokes vernacular domestic shelter. This is an imagined setting, not an architectural record of a named community's house.
artworks.alt: Rain-laden water droplets along the edge of a thatched Odisha veranda, soft teal pond beyond, an ochre woven mat rolled in the corner, no people.

artworks.title: The hour the stone remembers
artworks.caption: The carved chariot wheels of the Sun Temple at Konark are the reference. The generated close study is interpretive, not measured archaeological documentation.
artworks.alt: A close artistic study of a carved chariot wheel at Konark with weathered stone and warm side light.

artworks.title: The river takes its time
artworks.caption: An imagined Odisha river landscape; no precise river, village or conservation condition is asserted.
artworks.alt: A quiet bend in a broad Odisha river viewed from a high ochre bank, pale ivory mist, deep teal river ribbon and a distant modest fishing boat, no identifiable monument.

artworks.title: A small place to begin
artworks.caption: An everyday act of home growing and reuse, offered as a contemporary narrative rather than a named heritage practice.
artworks.alt: A small terracotta bowl with soaked rice seedlings on a wet courtyard ledge, muted sea-blue background and ivory cloudy light, realistic rural Odisha seasonal still life.

artworks.title: The shade knows everyone
artworks.caption: A tamarind tree as a shared village landscape; the story is imagined and does not document a particular meeting place.
artworks.alt: A large tamarind tree shading an empty red-earth path in rural Odisha, weathered ochre bench, soft pale summer haze, deep teal foliage shade.

artworks.title: A little sky indoors
artworks.caption: A domestic still life of water, metal and flower; no prescribed religious symbolism is assigned.
artworks.alt: An old brass bowl filled with clear water and one ivory flower on a laterite ledge, sea-blue reflected sky, delicate natural light, minimal Odisha domestic still life.

artworks.title: Where the hills exhale
artworks.caption: Deomali in Koraput, within the Eastern Ghats, is the geographical reference. This generated landscape is an artistic interpretation, not a location photograph.
artworks.alt: Broad grass-covered Deomali ridges beneath moving clouds, with layered hills beyond.

artworks.title: A world held in a thread
artworks.caption: Cuttack's tarakasi, or silver filigree, provides the craft reference. The generated ornament is an original interpretation, not a documented maker's piece.
artworks.alt: A single delicate Odisha-style silver filigree leaf earring resting on deep teal cotton with an ivory thread and a warm ochre wooden tabletop, restrained macro still life, no text.

artworks.title: The sea, held close
artworks.caption: A shore-found shell as a poetic object; this image makes no claim about a species, collection practice or ritual conch.
artworks.alt: A single conch shell beside the gentle foam line of an empty Odisha beach at winter sunrise, sea blue, ivory foam, muted ochre sand and soft rust horizon.

artworks.title: Enough to share
artworks.caption: Grain baskets connect woven utility, food and household memory; no specific basket tradition or community is asserted.
artworks.alt: Small woven bamboo grain baskets beneath a thatched rural Odisha veranda, ivory husks, ochre straw and a distant deep sea-blue door, quiet winter evening.

artworks.title: Before the first line
artworks.caption: An imagined writer's everyday table, opening the collection through attention rather than a biographical claim about an actual poet.
artworks.alt: A fresh small terracotta cup on an ivory cotton cloth beside an open unmarked notebook, sea-blue wooden table near a rural Odisha window, soft morning light, no visible writing.

artworks.title: LIFE AS IT IS
artworks.caption: LIFE AS IT IS
artworks.alt: A rain-washed earthen courtyard opens onto a pond and green fields; an indigo doorway, brass vessel and white threshold drawing suggest a quiet Odisha home.

artworks.title: A gift, opened
artworks.caption: A gift, opened
artworks.alt: A loosely opened paper packet of dates rests on a pale wooden table, with soft light falling from the left.

artworks.title: A way back
artworks.caption: A way back
artworks.alt: Worn steps descend from a grassy riverbank into quiet gray-green water beneath an overcast sky.
